items.title: Ini Alasan Vaksin Covid-19 Tidak Mungkin Disusupi Microchip
items.snippet_en: CNBC Indonesia explains why COVID-19 vaccines cannot contain microchips, citing the impossibility of injecting them due to size and the need for power and an antenna. This debunks the conspiracy theory.

items.title: KELIRU: Konten tentang Pemasangan Microchip Melalui Vaksinasi di Indonesia
items.snippet_en: Tempo.co debunks the claim that microchips are implanted through vaccination in Indonesia, stating it is false. This aligns with other sources refuting the microchip conspiracy theory.

items.title: FACTCHECK: COVID vaccines do not contain microchips
items.snippet_en: Amsterdam News fact-checks and confirms that COVID-19 vaccines do not contain microchips. Experts state that microchips are too large to be injected with vaccine needles and require power and an antenna.

items.title: Ingredients
items.snippet_en: FactCheck.org states that the ingredients of COVID-19 vaccines are publicly available and do not include microchips, debunking the claim that vaccines contain tracking devices.

items.title: 8 coronavirus vaccine myths debunked, from microchipping to mandates
items.snippet_en: Business Insider debunks several coronavirus vaccine myths, including the claim of microchipping. The article confirms that vaccine ingredients do not include microchips.

items.title: Facts about COVID-19 Vaccines
items.snippet_en: The CDC provides facts about COVID-19 vaccines, indicating that their ingredients are known and do not include microchips. This contradicts the claim of microchip inclusion.

items.title: Debunking COVID-19 (Coronavirus) Myths
items.snippet_en: MyMLC.com debunks COVID-19 myths, specifically addressing whether vaccines contain microchips. It states that vaccine ingredients do not include microchips, refuting the claim.

items.title: COVID-19 queries: Altered DNA and microchips
items.snippet_en: Mayo Clinic addresses queries about COVID-19 vaccines, including the microchip claim. It clarifies that vaccines do not contain microchips and that the theory may stem from misinterpretations of digital vaccine records.

items.title: Coronavirus myths
items.snippet_en: Mayo Clinic addresses coronavirus myths, including the false claim that COVID-19 vaccines contain microchips. This source contributes to debunking the conspiracy theory.

items.title: TRUST INDEX: Does the COVID-19 vaccine contain a tracking device?
items.snippet_en: KSAT's Trust Index investigates whether COVID-19 vaccines contain tracking devices and concludes that they do not. This supports the debunking of the microchip claim.

This YouTube video likely contributes to debunking the microchip claim, as it is cited alongside sources explaining the impossibility of microchips in vaccines due to size and functional requirements.

items.title: Where did the microchip vaccine conspiracy theory come from, anyway?
items.snippet_en: Reveal News investigates the origin of the microchip vaccine conspiracy theory, indicating its false nature. This source contributes to the overall debunking of the claim.

items.title: 20% of Americans believe microchips in COVID-19 vaccines: YouGov
items.snippet_en: Business Insider reports that a YouGov poll found 20% of Americans believe in microchips in COVID-19 vaccines, highlighting the prevalence of the debunked conspiracy theory.
AFP Fact Check likely debunks the claim that COVID-19 vaccines contain microchips, as it is listed among multiple sources refuting this conspiracy theory.

items.title: Jangan Percaya 4 Hoaks Vaksin COVID-19 Ini
items.snippet_en: Halodoc advises against believing four COVID-19 vaccine hoaxes, including the microchip claim. It states that vaccine ingredients do not include microchips.

items.title: Medfact: Vaksin Sinovac Mengandung Chip Pemantau? Ini Faktanya
items.snippet_en: KlikDokter addresses the claim that Sinovac vaccine contains tracking chips, stating the facts that refute this. This contributes to debunking the microchip conspiracy theory.

items.title: HOAX: Vaksin COVID-19 Mengandung Mikrocip Magnetis
items.snippet_en: The Indonesian Ministry of Health (Kemkes.go.id) explicitly labels the claim that COVID-19 vaccines contain magnetic microchips as a hoax, directly contradicting the user's claim.

items.title: VAKSIN BERISI ROBOT NANO DAN CHIP RFID
items.snippet_en: Jabarprov.go.id clarifies that claims of vaccines containing nano-robots and RFID chips are false. The theory gained traction due to misinterpretations of barcode-like chips for inventory.

items.title: COVID-19 Vaccines Don’t Have Patient-Tracking Devices
items.snippet_en: FactCheck.org confirms that COVID-19 vaccines do not contain patient-tracking devices. The theory is partly due to misinterpretations of digital vaccine records.

items.title: Microchip Bukti Vaksin COVID-19 Ditanam ke Tangan Manusia
items.snippet_en: Detik.com discusses a Swedish company's subdermal microchip developed in December 2021 to store COVID-19 vaccination data. It clarifies that this is not part of the vaccine itself and cannot track location.
